name: Helicopter tours in Nepal
tagline: Everest, Annapurna, Muktinath and Kailash by helicopter
meta_description: Helicopter tours in Nepal to Everest, Annapurna, Muktinath, Gosaikunda, Pathibhara and Kailash, with honest prices, weather rules and charter options.
summary: Nepal's helicopter tours put you at Everest's Kala Patthar (5,644 m), Annapurna Base Camp or Muktinath temple and back within a morning. We arrange shared seats from about US$1,100 for Everest and full charters for families, pilgrims and photographers, always flying early to beat the cloud that builds by midday.
intro: The Everest helicopter tour is our most requested flight. It leaves Kathmandu around 6:30 am, refuels at Lukla (2,860 m), lands for 10–15 minutes at Kala Patthar (5,644 m) or near Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), then stops for breakfast at Hotel Everest View (3,880 m) facing Ama Dablam. The round trip takes 4–5 hours. From Pokhara, the Annapurna Base Camp flight reaches the glacier amphitheatre at 4,130 m in about 25 minutes. From Kathmandu, the Langtang valley (Kyanjin Gompa, 3,870 m) and the sacred lake of Gosaikunda (4,380 m) are each 30–45 minutes away, which suits travellers with a single free morning.

Pilgrim flights make up much of the rest. Muktinath (3,710 m) is about 25 minutes from Pokhara, and a shared seat usually costs ₹45,000–65,000 with around an hour on the ground for darshan. Pathibhara Devi in Taplejung and Halesi Mahadev in Khotang are often flown together from Kathmandu in one long day. Further west, Rara Lake (2,990 m) is a short hop from Nepalgunj, while Manaslu flights land at Samagaun (3,530 m) inside a restricted area. For Kailash, groups fly Nepalgunj to Simikot by plane, then shuttle by helicopter to Hilsa on the Tibet border in sorties of about 20 minutes each.

The Everest mountain flight is different: a plane such as a Beechcraft 1900 or ATR 72 flies for about an hour along the range from Kathmandu without landing, and every passenger gets a window. Helicopters land, so they follow stricter rules. Flights go early because cloud usually builds by 11 am. At high landings an AS350 B3 helicopter carries fewer people, so a group of five may land in two lifts. A shared seat is cheapest; a private charter of up to five seats (US$5,000–6,500 for Everest) fixes the timing and the landing plan. Heli landing rules change, so check current status before you travel.

how_to_choose.title: Shared seat or private charter
how_to_choose.text: A shared seat suits couples and solo travellers on a budget: you fly with other passengers on a fixed morning slot. A charter costs more but suits families of four or five, pilgrims who need longer at a temple, and photographers who want to choose the landing and the light. We quote both for every route.

how_to_choose.title: Be honest about your health
how_to_choose.text: Landing above 5,000 m means thin air within an hour of leaving Kathmandu. We advise against high landings for anyone with heart or lung conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure or pregnancy, and for infants. These travellers can still enjoy breakfast at Hotel Everest View (3,880 m) or take the mountain flight instead.

how_to_choose.title: Keep one spare morning
how_to_choose.text: Mountain weather decides the schedule, not the clock. We plan every helicopter tour for the first clear slot after sunrise and ask you to keep the next morning free in case cloud, wind or a closed airstrip grounds the flight. Spring and autumn give the best odds; the monsoon months give the worst.

how_to_choose.title: Check weight and luggage limits
how_to_choose.text: Helicopters carry less as they climb. Operators weigh passengers and bags, may cap individual weight and allow only a small day pack on most tours. On Kailash and Muktinath shuttles, heavier groups fly in extra rotations, so share accurate weights with us when you book. Rules vary by operator; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does an Everest helicopter tour cost from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: A shared seat on an Everest helicopter tour with a landing at Kala Patthar or near Base Camp usually costs US$1,100–1,400 per person. A private charter for up to five people costs about US$5,000–6,500 per helicopter. Most packages include the breakfast stop at Hotel Everest View, while national park and municipality fees may be extra. Prices move with fuel costs and season.

faqs.q: Is the Everest mountain flight the same as a helicopter tour?
faqs.a: No. The Everest mountain flight is a scheduled plane, usually a Beechcraft 1900 or ATR 72, that leaves Kathmandu at dawn, flies east along the Himalaya for about an hour and returns without landing. Foreign nationals usually pay around US$200–250. It costs a fraction of a helicopter tour and suits children, seniors and anyone who should not go to high altitude. Fares vary by airline and nationality.

faqs.q: Why can't all five passengers land at Kala Patthar together?
faqs.a: Thin air reduces lift, so a helicopter that carries five passengers out of Kathmandu can safely carry fewer at 5,644 m. Pilots often drop part of the group lower down, land the first group at altitude, then return for the rest, or land everyone at a lower point. The pilot makes the final call on the day, based on weight, wind and temperature.

faqs.q: What happens if bad weather cancels my helicopter flight?
faqs.a: We move you to the next clear morning, which is why we ask you to keep a spare day. If cloud closes in during the flight, the pilot may shorten the route, skip a landing or turn back. How a cancelled or shortened flight is refunded depends on the operator and the terms in your booking, so read them before you pay.

faqs.q: How long does the Muktinath helicopter tour from Pokhara take?
faqs.a: Allow about 3 hours from hotel to hotel. The flight from Pokhara to Muktinath takes around 25 minutes each way, sometimes with a short stop at Jomsom, and you get roughly an hour at the temple, which is a short, steep walk up from the landing area. Shared seats usually cost ₹45,000–65,000. Flights from Kathmandu take longer and cost more.

faqs.q: How does the Simikot to Hilsa helicopter work for Kailash?
faqs.a: Groups fly Nepalgunj to Simikot (2,910 m) on a small plane, then take a helicopter of about 20 minutes to Hilsa on the Tibet border and cross to Purang the same day. Helicopters shuttle four or five passengers at a time, so a group of twenty needs several rotations, all weather dependent. Kailash rules for Indian passport holders change; check current status before you travel.

name: Trekking in Nepal
tagline: Teahouse treks from 4 days to 3 weeks with licensed guides
meta_description: Trekking in Nepal: Everest Base Camp, Annapurna, Langtang and Manaslu treks with licensed guides, permits, seasons, grades and realistic prices.
summary: Nepal's main trekking seasons are October–November and March–May. We organise guided teahouse treks from the 4-day Poon Hill loop to the 12–14 day Everest Base Camp trek (US$1,300–1,800) and the Manaslu circuit, with permits, licensed guides, acclimatisation days and Lukla flights built into the plan.
intro: Most treks in Nepal are teahouse treks: you walk 5–7 hours a day between villages and sleep in simple lodges with dal bhat on the menu. The Everest Base Camp trek takes 12–14 days from Kathmandu, climbs to Kala Patthar (5,644 m) and usually costs US$1,300–1,800 with Lukla flights. The Annapurna Base Camp trek takes 10–12 days, tops out at 4,130 m and costs about US$750–1,100. Shorter options include Ghorepani Poon Hill (3,210 m) in 4–5 days from Pokhara and the Langtang valley in 7–9 days, reached by road from Kathmandu.

Longer routes cross high passes. The Annapurna Circuit climbs over Thorong La (5,416 m) between Manang and Muktinath in 12–16 days. The Manaslu circuit crosses Larkya La at about 5,100 m and needs a restricted area permit, a minimum of two trekkers and a licensed guide. Since 2023 Nepal has required foreign trekkers on most national park and conservation area routes to walk with a licensed guide, and park entry permits are checked along the trail. Permit fees and guide rules change, so check current status before you travel.

Altitude is the main risk, not fitness. Above 3,000 m we plan to raise your sleeping height by no more than 300–500 m a day and add a rest day for every 1,000 m or so, such as two nights at Namche Bazaar (3,440 m) and another at Dingboche. Headache, nausea and poor sleep are early signs of acute mountain sickness; the cure is to stop climbing or descend. October and November give the clearest views, spring brings rhododendrons, and the June–September monsoon brings leeches, cloud and flight delays on most routes.

how_to_choose.title: Pick the length you can spare
how_to_choose.text: Count the days you have, then subtract one buffer day for flights, especially to Lukla. With 5–6 days, Poon Hill or Mardi Himal fit; with 10–12, Annapurna Base Camp or Langtang; with 14 or more, Everest Base Camp, Gokyo or the Annapurna and Manaslu circuits.

how_to_choose.title: Match the grade to your fitness
how_to_choose.text: Easy and moderate treks need no experience, just 4–6 hours a day of walking on uneven stone steps. Challenging routes add long days above 4,500 m and a high pass. Train for six to eight weeks with stairs, hill walks and a loaded day pack, and you will enjoy the trail far more.

how_to_choose.title: Decide on simple lodges or comfort
how_to_choose.text: Standard teahouses have twin rooms, shared toilets and charging for a fee. On the Everest trail, Yeti Mountain Home lodges add attached bathrooms and better beds for a higher price. Annapurna lodges are simpler but closer together. Tell us your comfort level and we plan the overnight stops around it.

how_to_choose.title: Plan permits and insurance early
how_to_choose.text: Restricted areas such as Manaslu, Upper Mustang and Tsum Valley need a special permit arranged through a registered agency with your passport details. Every trekker should carry insurance that covers helicopter evacuation up to at least 6,000 m. Indian nationals still need permits, though fees differ by nationality; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time for trekking in Nepal?
faqs.a: October and November are the best months for most treks: stable weather, clear mountain views and mild days, though trails are busiest. March to May is the second season, warmer and hazier, with rhododendrons in bloom below 3,500 m. December to February suits lower treks such as Poon Hill. June to September is monsoon, best only for rain-shadow areas like Upper Mustang.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide to trek in Nepal?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Since April 2023 Nepal has required foreign trekkers in national parks and conservation areas to hire a licensed guide, and restricted areas have always needed one. Some local authorities, including in Khumbu, have applied the rule differently, so check current status before you travel. We build a licensed guide into every trek quote; porters are optional, usually one for every two trekkers.

faqs.q: How much does a trek in Nepal cost?
faqs.a: A guided Poon Hill trek of 4–5 days costs roughly US$350–550 per person from Pokhara. Annapurna Base Camp runs about US$750–1,100 for 10–12 days, and Everest Base Camp about US$1,300–1,800 for 12–14 days including Lukla flights. Prices usually cover guide, permits, lodges and trail meals; drinks, hot showers, charging and tips are usually extra.

faqs.q: How fit do I need to be for the Everest Base Camp trek?
faqs.a: You do not need climbing experience, but you should be able to walk 5–7 hours on steep, rocky trail for several days in a row. The hardest part is the altitude above 4,000 m, where every step feels slower. Six to eight weeks of hill walking, stair climbing and cardio three or four times a week is enough for most healthy adults.

faqs.q: Can Indians trek in Nepal without a passport?
faqs.a: Indian nationals can enter Nepal with a Voter ID card instead of a passport, and that is usually enough for trekking permits on routes such as Annapurna and Everest. Restricted area permits for Manaslu or Upper Mustang may require passport details, so carry a valid passport if you plan a remote route. Permit fees for SAARC nationals are lower; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What should I do if I get altitude sickness on a trek?
faqs.a: Stop climbing at the first signs: headache, nausea, loss of appetite or poor sleep. Rest a day at the same height, drink water and tell your guide. If symptoms get worse, or you feel confused or breathless at rest, descend at least 300–500 m straight away. Severe cases need a helicopter evacuation, which is why insurance covering rescue is essential.

name: Cultural tours of Nepal
tagline: Temples, old towns and living traditions across Nepal
meta_description: Cultural tours of Nepal covering Kathmandu, Patan, Bhaktapur, Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Bandipur and Janakpur, with guides, prices and best months.
summary: Nepal's cultural heart is the Kathmandu Valley, where seven UNESCO-listed monument zones sit within about 20 km of each other. We run cultural tours from 3 nights in Kathmandu (₹14,000–25,000) to 6–8 night circuits adding Bandipur, Pokhara, Tansen or Janakpur, with guides who explain the Hindu, Buddhist and Newar history behind each site.
intro: The Kathmandu Valley is the core of any cultural tour. Its UNESCO World Heritage listing covers seven monument zones: the Durbar Squares of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur, the stupas of Swayambhunath and Boudhanath, the Pashupatinath temple complex and Changu Narayan, regarded as one of Nepal's oldest temples. A 3-night Kathmandu break at a 3-star hotel usually costs ₹14,000–25,000 per person and covers five or six of them with a guide. Much was damaged in the 2015 earthquake; most temples have been rebuilt, and restoration work is still visible in Bhaktapur and Kathmandu Durbar Square.

Beyond the valley, Newar trading towns keep their brick lanes and carved wooden windows. Bandipur, on a ridge at about 1,030 m between Kathmandu and Pokhara, keeps cars out of its main bazaar. Tansen, on the hill road between Lumbini and Pokhara, has a Newar bazaar and the Bhagwati temple. Gorkha has the hilltop palace where Prithvi Narayan Shah began uniting Nepal in the 18th century. In the Terai, Janakpur's white Janaki Mandir honours Sita and draws large crowds at Vivah Panchami in November or December. A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan circuit with one of these stops costs about ₹28,000–45,000 at 3-star.

Many of these places are working temples and neighbourhoods. Morning puja at Pashupatinath, butter lamps around Boudhanath at dusk and potters drying clay in Bhaktapur's Pottery Square happen whether visitors come or not. The best months are October to April, when festivals such as Dashain, Tihar and Bisket Jatra fill the squares; monsoon tours still work, as most sites are paved and close to the road. Entry fees for the Durbar Squares are lower for SAARC nationals, including Indians, than for other visitors. Fees and opening hours change, so check current status before you travel.

how_to_choose.title: Choose how many towns to see
how_to_choose.text: Three nights covers the Kathmandu Valley well: one day for Kathmandu and Patan, one for Bhaktapur with Changu Narayan, and one for Pashupatinath with Boudhanath. Add Bandipur, Gorkha or Tansen for Newar hill towns, or Janakpur for Mithila art and the Ramayana link. More than one move every two nights gets tiring.

how_to_choose.title: Hire a licensed heritage guide
how_to_choose.text: A good guide turns carved struts and courtyards into stories about Malla kings, Newar guilds and the rituals still performed there. We use government-licensed guides for cultural sightseeing days. Ask us for a guide who speaks Hindi, English or your own language, and say which topics interest you most, from architecture to food.

how_to_choose.title: Stay inside the old towns
how_to_choose.text: Sleeping in a heritage guesthouse inside Bhaktapur or Patan lets you see the squares at dawn before day visitors arrive. Options range from guesthouses in restored Newar houses to Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu, which is built around salvaged carved woodwork. Budget at least one night in an old town.

how_to_choose.title: Time your trip with a festival
how_to_choose.text: Festivals bring out masked dances, chariot pulls and family rituals you will not see on an ordinary day. Indra Jatra in August or September, Dashain and Tihar between September and November, and Bisket Jatra in mid-April are the big ones in the valley. Dates follow the lunar calendar, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for a Kathmandu cultural tour?
faqs.a: Three full days is the right amount for the Kathmandu Valley. That covers Kathmandu Durbar Square and Swayambhunath, Patan, Bhaktapur with Changu Narayan or Nagarkot, and Pashupatinath with Boudhanath at a steady pace. With two days you can see the main five sites but will rush. A 3-night package at a 3-star hotel usually costs ₹14,000–25,000 per person.

faqs.q: Can non-Hindus enter Pashupatinath temple?
faqs.a: Non-Hindus cannot enter the main Pashupatinath temple courtyard, but they can walk the riverbank ghats, the hillside shrines and the terraces across the Bagmati, from where the temple roofs and cremation platforms are visible. Hindu visitors, including Indians, can enter for darshan. Photography of cremations should be discreet, and no photos are allowed inside the main temple.

faqs.q: What is the entry fee for Bhaktapur Durbar Square for Indians?
faqs.a: SAARC nationals, including Indians, pay a lower rate than other foreigners at Bhaktapur, Patan and Kathmandu Durbar Squares, but they still pay; only Nepali citizens enter free. Fees have been revised several times in recent years, so we quote them separately or include them in your package. Keep your ticket, as checkpoints in Bhaktapur ask to see it. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Nepal suitable for a cultural tour with elderly parents?
faqs.a: Yes, with sensible planning. The Kathmandu Valley sits at about 1,400 m, so altitude is not an issue, and most heritage sites are fairly flat apart from the steps at Swayambhunath, where a car can reach the top, and Changu Narayan. We suggest a private car rather than a coach, sightseeing days of 4–5 hours and hotels with lifts. Winter mornings can drop to 2–3 °C.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur?
faqs.a: All three were Malla-era royal cities with their own Durbar Squares. Kathmandu's square is the busiest, home to the Kumari Ghar and the old Hanuman Dhoka palace. Patan is known for metalwork, its stone Krishna Mandir and the Patan Museum. Bhaktapur is the best preserved, with the 55-Window Palace, the five-tiered Nyatapola temple and pottery workshops, and it is quieter in the evenings.

faqs.q: Which cultural sites in Nepal are outside Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, is the most important, about 8–9 hours by road or a 35-minute flight plus a short drive. Bandipur and Tansen are preserved Newar hill towns, Gorkha has the palace of Prithvi Narayan Shah, and Janakpur has the Janaki Mandir. In the mountains, Lo Manthang in Upper Mustang has walled-city monasteries with 15th-century murals.

name: Pilgrimage tours in Nepal
tagline: Pashupatinath, Muktinath, Janakpur and the sacred lakes
meta_description: Pilgrimage tours in Nepal to Pashupatinath, Muktinath, Manakamana, Janakpur, Gosaikunda and Pathibhara by road, flight or helicopter, with prices.
summary: Hindu pilgrimage tours in Nepal centre on Pashupatinath in Kathmandu and Muktinath (3,710 m) in Mustang, with Manakamana, Janakpur, Gosaikunda, Pathibhara and Halesi as popular additions. We plan yatras by road, flight or helicopter, with darshan timings, puja arrangements, vegetarian meals and the gentle pace that older pilgrims need.
intro: Pashupatinath, on the Bagmati in Kathmandu, is the starting point for most Indian pilgrims and the main stage for Maha Shivaratri each February or March. From there the classic yatra heads west. Manakamana temple, reached by a cable car ride of about 10 minutes from Kurintar on the Kathmandu–Pokhara road, is a stop for wish-fulfilling darshan. Pokhara is the base for Muktinath, sacred to Vishnu and Shiva and counted among the 108 Divya Desams, where pilgrims bathe under 108 water spouts. The temple sits at 3,710 m, so it is reached by flight, jeep or helicopter rather than an ordinary car.

There are three ways to reach Muktinath. The cheapest is by jeep from Pokhara via Beni and Jomsom, about 190 km and 8–10 hours each way on a rough mountain road. The second is a 20-minute flight from Pokhara to Jomsom (2,720 m), then a jeep of about 1.5 hours. The fastest is a helicopter from Pokhara, about 25 minutes each way, usually ₹45,000–65,000 per seat. Jomsom flights only operate in the morning and are often delayed by wind. A 5–6 night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Muktinath yatra by road starts at around ₹30,000–45,000 per person at 3-star.

Other pilgrimages need more planning. Janakpur, the birthplace of Sita, is easiest from Bihar and fills up at Vivah Panchami in November or December. Gosaikunda lake (4,380 m) in Langtang draws thousands at Janai Purnima in August, when the trail is wet and crowded; many pilgrims now fly in by helicopter. In eastern Nepal, Pathibhara Devi (about 3,794 m) above Taplejung and the cave temple of Halesi Mahadev in Khotang are often combined by helicopter. Festival dates follow the lunar calendar and helicopter landing rules change, so check current status before you travel.

how_to_choose.title: Choose road, flight or helicopter
how_to_choose.text: Road yatras cost least but involve long drives on mountain roads; flights save days but depend on morning weather; helicopters cost most but let seniors reach Muktinath or Gosaikunda in under an hour. Many families mix them, driving to Pokhara and flying the final high section to Jomsom or Muktinath.

how_to_choose.title: Plan for altitude at Muktinath
how_to_choose.text: Muktinath is higher than Kedarnath or Badrinath. Climbing straight from Pokhara (822 m) to 3,710 m can cause headaches and breathlessness, so walk slowly, drink water and keep your time on top to around an hour if you fly in. Pilgrims with heart or lung conditions should consult a doctor first.

how_to_choose.title: Book around festival dates
how_to_choose.text: Maha Shivaratri at Pashupatinath, Janai Purnima at Gosaikunda and Vivah Panchami at Janakpur bring huge crowds, higher hotel rates and road closures near temples. They are also the most rewarding days to be there. Book rooms two to three months ahead, or travel a week either side for calmer darshan.

how_to_choose.title: Ask for vegetarian and puja support
how_to_choose.text: Most Indian pilgrims want pure vegetarian meals, sometimes without onion and garlic, and help arranging a puja or rudrabhishek with a priest. Tell us your needs when booking. Hotels in Kathmandu, Pokhara and Jomsom can usually manage, while simple lodges near Muktinath have limited menus.

faqs.q: What is the cost of a Pashupatinath and Muktinath tour from India?
faqs.a: A 5–6 night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Muktinath yatra by road and jeep usually costs ₹30,000–45,000 per person at 3-star, twin sharing, starting in Kathmandu. Adding Pokhara–Jomsom flights raises it by roughly ₹12,000–20,000, and a Muktinath helicopter from Pokhara costs ₹45,000–65,000 per seat. Travel from your Indian city to Kathmandu is extra.

faqs.q: Can senior citizens visit Muktinath?
faqs.a: Yes, many pilgrims in their 60s and 70s reach Muktinath each season. The safest way is a helicopter from Pokhara, or a Jomsom flight with a night in Jomsom (2,720 m) to adjust. From the parking or landing area there is a short uphill walk to the temple, and ponies are usually available. Anyone with heart, lung or blood pressure problems should get medical advice first.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Muktinath?
faqs.a: March to May and September to November are best, with clear mornings and open roads. Winter, from December to February, is cold, often below freezing, and snow can close the road and ground flights. In the June–August monsoon, Mustang itself stays fairly dry, but the road below Jomsom suffers landslides and Pokhara–Jomsom flights are often cancelled.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to visit Muktinath?
faqs.a: Muktinath lies in the Annapurna Conservation Area, so visitors other than Nepali citizens need an ACAP entry permit, which we arrange in Pokhara or Kathmandu. Indian nationals pay a lower SAARC rate. Lower Mustang, including Muktinath, does not need the restricted area permit required for Upper Mustang beyond Kagbeni. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I reach Gosaikunda for Janai Purnima?
faqs.a: Most pilgrims drive from Kathmandu to Dhunche, about 120 km and 5–6 hours, then walk two to three days via Chandanbari to Gosaikunda at 4,380 m. The trail is steep, wet and crowded in August. A helicopter from Kathmandu takes 30–40 minutes and is the only practical option for older pilgrims, weather permitting. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I combine Pathibhara and Halesi in one trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Pathibhara Devi in Taplejung and Halesi Mahadev in Khotang are both in eastern Nepal and are often combined in a single-day helicopter tour from Kathmandu, weather permitting. By road the pair takes about a week, with long drives and a steep walk of several hours up to Pathibhara. Time on the ground at each temple is limited on helicopter tours.

name: Wildlife safaris in Nepal
tagline: Rhinos, tigers and gharials in Chitwan and Bardia
meta_description: Wildlife safaris in Nepal: Chitwan and Bardia packages for rhinos, tigers and birds, with seasons, lodges, travel times and prices from ₹12,000.
summary: Nepal's lowland parks hold greater one-horned rhinos, Bengal tigers, gharial crocodiles and more than 500 bird species. Chitwan is 5–6 hours from Kathmandu and suits a 2–3 night safari from ₹12,000–20,000; Bardia, in the far west, is wilder and better for tiger tracking. October to April is the best season.
intro: Chitwan National Park, Nepal's first, covers about 950 sq km of sal forest and grassland along the Rapti and Narayani rivers. Sauraha, on its northern edge, is the main base, about 165 km and 5–6 hours by road from Kathmandu or a 25-minute flight to Bharatpur. A standard 2-night package at ₹12,000–20,000 includes a jeep safari, a dugout canoe trip on the Rapti looking for mugger and gharial crocodiles, a jungle walk with naturalists and a Tharu cultural show. Rhinos are seen on most jeep drives; tigers are possible but never guaranteed.

Bardia National Park, around 968 sq km on the Karnali river, is Chitwan's quieter counterpart. It is about 95 km and 2.5–3 hours from Nepalgunj, which has flights from Kathmandu and a road border with India at Rupaidiha. Bardia has fewer lodges, fewer vehicles and good tiger sighting chances, especially from February to May when the tall grass has been cut and animals come to the rivers. Full-day jeep drives and walking safaris are the norm. Nepal's 2022 national survey counted 355 tigers, up from about 121 in 2009.

Smaller parks reward specialists. Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve in the east is a winter stop for migratory waterbirds and home to Nepal's last wild water buffalo, the arna. Shuklaphanta National Park in the far west has large herds of swamp deer on open grassland. October to March is cool and pleasant, with misty mornings in December and January; April to June is hot, often above 35 °C, but wildlife viewing peaks. Many lodges near Chitwan stay open through the monsoon, though park activities are reduced from July to September. Check current status before you travel.

how_to_choose.title: Chitwan or Bardia
how_to_choose.text: Choose Chitwan for a first safari, easy road and air access from Kathmandu or Pokhara, and a wide choice of hotels. Choose Bardia if tigers are your priority and you are happy with simpler lodges, longer days in the jeep and a flight to Nepalgunj or a drive from the Rupaidiha border.

how_to_choose.title: Stay at least two nights
how_to_choose.text: One night in Chitwan gives you barely half a day of activities after the drive. Two nights allow a jeep safari, the canoe trip and a dawn walk; three nights add a full-day jeep drive deep into the park, which is where tiger and sloth bear sightings become more likely.

how_to_choose.title: Pick the right season
how_to_choose.text: October to March has the most comfortable weather and the best birding. February to May, after the grass cutting, gives the clearest views of rhino and tiger, but April and May are hot. In the monsoon, rivers rise, some areas close and leeches appear on forest walks.

how_to_choose.title: Choose your lodge style
how_to_choose.text: Sauraha has budget and mid-range hotels within walking distance of the river. Lodges such as Barahi Jungle Lodge, Kasara Resort and Meghauli Serai add naturalist teams, pools and better food at higher prices. In Bardia, family-run lodges near Thakurdwara offer simple rooms and experienced trackers.

faqs.q: How much does a Chitwan safari package cost from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: A 2-night Chitwan package usually costs ₹12,000–20,000 per person at a standard Sauraha hotel, twin sharing, including meals, a jeep safari, canoe ride, jungle walk and park fees. A private car from Kathmandu adds roughly ₹8,000–12,000 per vehicle each way. Luxury jungle lodges cost several times more but include naturalists and full-day drives.

faqs.q: What are the chances of seeing a tiger in Chitwan?
faqs.a: On a short stay, low. Most visitors to Chitwan see rhinos, deer, crocodiles and many birds, but tigers are shy and the forest is dense. A full-day jeep safari deep into the park, or a trip to Bardia between February and May, improves the odds considerably. No responsible operator can guarantee a tiger sighting.

faqs.q: Is a Chitwan safari suitable for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Sauraha sits at about 150 m, so altitude is no issue, and jeep safaris, canoe rides and the elephant breeding centre suit most ages. Jungle walks are better for children over about 10, as they require silence and staying close to the guide. In April and May, plan activities for early morning and late afternoon to avoid the heat.

faqs.q: Can I visit Chitwan in the monsoon?
faqs.a: You can, but expect limits. From about July to September heavy rain, high rivers and tall grass reduce jeep routes, and some lodges close. Leeches are common on walks. The upside is lower prices, green forest and fewer visitors. If you travel then, choose a lodge that stays open and keep your plans flexible. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I get to Bardia National Park?
faqs.a: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj in about an hour, then drive about 95 km to Thakurdwara on the edge of Bardia, roughly 2.5–3 hours. From India, the Rupaidiha–Nepalgunj border is about 180–190 km from Lucknow, so many Indian travellers drive straight in. By road from Kathmandu it is around 520 km and a long 12–14 hour day.

faqs.q: Are elephant rides still offered in Chitwan?
faqs.a: Elephant-back safaris have largely been phased out, and many lodges no longer offer them on welfare grounds. Jeep, canoe and walking safaris give better wildlife viewing anyway. You can still see elephants at the government breeding centre near Sauraha, and some lodges run elephant observation walks without riding. Policies change; check current status before you travel.

name: Adventure sports in Nepal
tagline: Paragliding, rafting, bungee and zipline in the Himalaya
meta_description: Adventure sports in Nepal: tandem paragliding in Pokhara, rafting on the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi, bungee and zipline, with ages, seasons and prices.
summary: Pokhara is Nepal's adventure base, with tandem paragliding from Sarangkot, a long zipline and ultralight flights over Phewa Lake. Rivers such as the Trishuli, Bhote Koshi and Sun Koshi offer rafting from easy day trips to multi-day expeditions. We combine adventure days with sightseeing, at prices that usually run ₹4,000–10,000 per activity.
intro: Tandem paragliding from Sarangkot (about 1,600 m) above Pokhara is Nepal's most popular adventure. Flights last 20–30 minutes, or about an hour on a cross-country option, and land beside Phewa Lake with Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range in view. Expect to pay roughly ₹6,000–10,000 including pick-up. The season runs from about October to May; operators stop flying in heavy monsoon rain and strong wind. No experience is needed, though there is usually a weight range for passengers. Pokhara also has a zipline that drops several hundred metres from Sarangkot towards the Seti valley, and ultralight aircraft flights over the lake.

Rafting is the other big draw. The Trishuli, about 2–3 hours west of Kathmandu on the Pokhara road, has Grade 3–4 rapids and makes an easy day trip or a stop on the way to Pokhara or Chitwan, from around ₹4,000–6,000. The Bhote Koshi near the Tibet border is steeper and colder, Grade 4–5, for fit swimmers. The Seti suits families and beginners, and the Sun Koshi and Karnali run for 7–10 days through remote gorges. October to December and March to May are the main rafting months, as monsoon levels make most rivers unsafe.

For pure adrenaline, a bungee jump over the Bhote Koshi gorge, about 3 hours from Kathmandu, has a drop of around 160 m, and Pokhara has a lower bungee tower. Canyoning, mountain biking on the Kathmandu Valley rim and kayaking clinics on the Seti round out the choice. Pick operators with trained guides, recent equipment checks and proper insurance, and check that your travel policy covers the activity. Adventure sites close or change after floods and landslides, especially after the monsoon, so check current status before you travel.

how_to_choose.title: Match the activity to your nerve
how_to_choose.text: Paragliding and a Trishuli rafting trip need no experience and suit nervous first-timers with a good guide. The zipline and bungee are short, intense and mostly mental. Grade 4–5 rivers such as the Bhote Koshi need confident swimmers. Start gentle and step up once you know how you react.

how_to_choose.title: Check age and weight limits
how_to_choose.text: Most operators set a minimum age of around 10–14 for rafting and bungee, and weight ranges for paragliding, zipline and bungee for safety reasons. Children can usually raft the Seti or the easier Trishuli stretches in a family boat. We confirm the exact rules with each operator before you book.

how_to_choose.title: Plan around weather and water
how_to_choose.text: Paragliding needs light winds and is best from October to April. Rafting rivers are at their best from October to December and again from March to May; monsoon floods close most stretches. Keep a flexible morning in Pokhara, as flights are often moved to the next day when wind picks up.

how_to_choose.title: Combine adventure with sightseeing
how_to_choose.text: Pokhara works well as a 3–4 night base: one morning paragliding, one afternoon on the zipline, plus boating on Phewa and sunrise at Sarangkot. Raft the Trishuli on the drive from Kathmandu, then continue to Pokhara or Chitwan the same day to save a night.

faqs.q: How much does paragliding cost in Pokhara?
faqs.a: A tandem paragliding flight from Sarangkot usually costs about ₹6,000–10,000 per person for 20–30 minutes in the air, including pick-up and the drive to the take-off point. Longer cross-country flights of about an hour cost more. Photos and videos from the pilot's camera are often extra. Prices are highest in October and November, when demand peaks.

faqs.q: Is paragliding in Pokhara safe?
faqs.a: Tandem paragliding in Pokhara has a reasonable safety record when you fly with a registered operator and a licensed pilot, but it is not risk-free and accidents do happen. Choose companies with up-to-date equipment and insurance, follow the pilot's briefing, and do not fly in strong wind or poor visibility. Pregnant women and people with back problems should not fly.

faqs.q: Which river is best for rafting in Nepal?
faqs.a: For a first trip, the Trishuli is the easiest choice: Grade 3–4 rapids, 2–3 hours from Kathmandu, and a simple add-on to a Pokhara or Chitwan tour. Thrill-seekers prefer the Bhote Koshi, Grade 4–5. For a multi-day expedition, the Sun Koshi or Karnali offer 7–10 days of camping on river beaches through remote canyons.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age for rafting in Nepal?
faqs.a: On easy Grade 2–3 stretches of the Trishuli or Seti, operators often accept children from about 8–10 years with a life jacket and a family boat. On Grade 4–5 rivers such as the Bhote Koshi, the usual minimum is 14–16, and confident swimming is required. Rules vary by operator, so we check before confirming your booking.

faqs.q: Can I do bungee jumping in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. The best-known jump drops about 160 m from a suspension bridge over the Bhote Koshi gorge, around 3 hours from Kathmandu near the Tibet border. Pokhara also has a lower bungee tower. Jumps include a briefing and safety checks, and there are age and weight limits. Floods have affected the Bhote Koshi valley in recent years, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best season for adventure sports in Nepal?
faqs.a: October and November are the best all-round months: clear skies for paragliding and good water levels for rafting. March to May is also good, warmer and slightly hazier. December to February is fine for paragliding and the zipline but cold on the river. From June to September, monsoon rain closes most rivers and limits flights.

name: Peak climbing in Nepal
tagline: Island Peak, Mera Peak and Lobuche East with climbing guides
meta_description: Peak climbing in Nepal: Island Peak, Mera Peak, Lobuche East and Himlung with permits, guides, seasons, training advice and prices from US$2,200.
summary: Peak climbing in Nepal starts with 6,000 m trekking peaks such as Island Peak (6,189 m), Mera Peak (6,476 m) and Lobuche East (6,119 m), climbed in 16–20 days with fixed ropes and crampons. We arrange permits, climbing guides, gear checks and acclimatisation, from around US$2,200 for Island Peak.
intro: Nepal's trekking peaks are the usual first step above 6,000 m. Island Peak (Imja Tse, 6,189 m) is climbed from Chhukung after acclimatising on the Everest Base Camp trail; summit day starts around 1–2 am, crosses a glacier and finishes on a steep fixed-rope headwall. Mera Peak (6,476 m), south of Everest, is higher but technically easier, a long glacier walk with views of five 8,000 m peaks. Lobuche East (6,119 m) is steeper and rockier. Most itineraries take 16–20 days from Kathmandu and cost roughly US$2,200–3,500 with a climbing guide.

In the Annapurna region, Pisang Peak (6,091 m) is climbed from the Annapurna Circuit, and the Chulu peaks rise above Manang. Above these sit the expedition peaks: Ama Dablam (6,812 m), a steep technical climb, and Himlung Himal (7,126 m), a popular first 7,000 m summit. Trekking peaks need a permit from the Nepal Mountaineering Association, while expedition peaks need a government permit with royalties, a liaison officer and higher insurance. Royalties vary by season and were revised recently, so check current status before you travel.

Spring (April to May) and autumn (October to November) are the climbing seasons, with autumn colder but clearer. You do not need previous mountaineering experience for Island Peak or Mera, but you should be a strong trekker who has been above 4,500 m comfortably, and you will practise with crampons, ice axe, jumar and descender at base camp before the summit. Expect 10–14 hour summit days. Insurance must cover climbing to the peak's altitude and helicopter rescue. Good boots, a down jacket and proper acclimatisation matter more than raw strength.

how_to_choose.title: Start with the right first peak
how_to_choose.text: Mera Peak suits strong trekkers who want height without steep ice. Island Peak adds a short, steep headwall on fixed ropes and pairs neatly with Everest Base Camp. Lobuche East is more technical and better as a second peak. Choose by your experience on snow, not by the altitude number.

how_to_choose.title: Allow enough acclimatisation
how_to_choose.text: Most failed summits come from rushing. A good trekking peak itinerary spends 10–12 days reaching base camp, often crossing a pass or climbing Kala Patthar first, and builds in a spare summit day for bad weather. Short itineraries look cheaper but cut the margin you need above 5,500 m.

how_to_choose.title: Check the guide ratio and gear
how_to_choose.text: On summit day you want one climbing guide for every one or two climbers, fixed ropes on the steep sections and a gear check before you leave Kathmandu. Boots, harnesses and crampons can be rented in Thamel, but bring your own if you have them and test everything before the trek.

how_to_choose.title: Budget for permits and extras
how_to_choose.text: Quotes should list the climbing permit, national park and municipality fees, garbage deposit, guide wages and summit bonus, and Lukla flights. Rescue insurance, rented gear, tips and extra nights after weather delays are usually extra. Fees change by season and year; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can a beginner climb Island Peak?
faqs.a: A fit beginner with no climbing experience can climb Island Peak with a good guide and proper acclimatisation, but it is not a walk-up. You must be comfortable trekking above 5,000 m, and you will learn to use crampons, an ice axe and a jumar on fixed ropes during a training day at base camp. Expect a 10–12 hour summit day.

faqs.q: Which is easier, Mera Peak or Island Peak?
faqs.a: Mera Peak is technically easier: mostly a long glacier walk with a short steep section near the top. Island Peak is lower at 6,189 m but has a steep headwall climbed on fixed ropes and a narrow summit ridge. Mera's challenge is its height, 6,476 m, and the remote approach through the Hinku valley, so acclimatisation matters more.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to climb Island Peak?
faqs.a: A guided Island Peak climb combined with the Everest Base Camp trek usually costs about US$2,200–3,200 per person for 16–19 days, including permits, Lukla flights, guide and lodges. Climbing gear rental, rescue insurance, tips and extra nights caused by weather are usually extra. Permit royalties are lower in autumn and winter than in spring.

faqs.q: What is the best season for peak climbing in Nepal?
faqs.a: April to May and October to November. Spring is slightly warmer and the most popular time on Everest-region peaks, though afternoon cloud is common. Autumn has clearer skies and colder summit mornings, often −15 to −25 °C with wind chill. Winter climbs are possible on some peaks but are very cold, and the monsoon brings heavy snow and poor visibility.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to climb a peak in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. Trekking peaks such as Island Peak, Mera and Lobuche East need a climbing permit from the Nepal Mountaineering Association, plus national park or conservation area fees and local municipality permits. Expedition peaks need a government permit and a liaison officer. Permits are issued through registered agencies, so we arrange them for you; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What training should I do before climbing a 6,000 m peak?
faqs.a: Build endurance for three months: long hill walks with a 10 kg pack, stair sessions and cardio four or five times a week. A basic snow and ice course, or a trek above 5,000 m such as Kala Patthar or Thorong La, is very useful. Practise walking in crampons and using a jumar before you go if you can.

name: Family holidays in Nepal
tagline: Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan at a child-friendly pace
meta_description: Family holidays in Nepal: Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan packages for children, with safe altitudes, travel times, best months and prices from ₹28,000.
summary: The classic Nepal family holiday is a 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan loop, costing about ₹28,000–45,000 per person at 3-star. It keeps everyone below 2,000 m, mixes temples with boating, a jeep safari and short hill walks, and uses private cars or 25-minute flights to avoid long days on the road.
intro: Most families start with two or three nights in Kathmandu, at about 1,400 m. Children tend to enjoy the pigeons and woodcarvings of Bhaktapur, the monkeys at Swayambhunath and the prayer wheels around Boudhanath more than formal museums. From Kathmandu, Pokhara is a 25-minute flight or a 200 km drive of 6–8 hours on a busy highway. At 822 m, Pokhara is relaxed and flat around Phewa Lake, with rowing boats, the International Mountain Museum, Davis Falls and an early drive up to Sarangkot for sunrise over Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range.

Chitwan adds the wildlife: a jeep safari for rhinos and deer, a canoe on the Rapti, the elephant breeding centre and Tharu dances in the evening. A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan holiday at 3-star typically costs ₹28,000–45,000 per person, twin sharing, and ₹95,000 or more at 5-star. Children sharing with parents are usually charged less. Nagarkot or Dhulikhel make a good one-night escape from Kathmandu for mountain views. For a look at the high Himalaya without altitude risk, the one-hour Everest mountain flight suits most children.

October to November and March to April are the easiest months, with mild days and clear views. December and January work too, but Kathmandu mornings can be 2–3 °C and Chitwan is foggy until mid-morning. Indian school holidays in May and June are hot in Chitwan, often above 35 °C, and Pokhara turns humid as the monsoon nears, but rates are lower. Keep altitude modest with young children: short treks to Australian Camp or Ghandruk stay at around 2,000 m and suit fit families in 2–3 days.

how_to_choose.title: Fly the long legs with small children
how_to_choose.text: The Kathmandu–Pokhara and Pokhara–Chitwan roads take 5–8 hours with traffic and roadworks. With children under eight, we suggest flying at least one leg: Kathmandu–Pokhara and Bharatpur–Kathmandu flights take about 25 minutes each. Older children usually cope well with one road day if there are regular stops.

how_to_choose.title: Keep the altitude gentle
how_to_choose.text: Children cannot always describe altitude symptoms, so keep overnight stays below about 2,500 m on a family trip. Kathmandu, Pokhara, Chitwan, Nagarkot and Bandipur are all lower. Short treks to Ghandruk or Australian Camp work well; leave Everest Base Camp until children are fit, trained teenagers.

how_to_choose.title: Choose hotels with space
how_to_choose.text: Family rooms, swimming pools and garden space make a big difference after a day of sightseeing. Pokhara's lakeside hotels and Chitwan's jungle resorts usually have more room than central Kathmandu hotels. Ask us for interconnecting or triple rooms; many 3-star hotels can add an extra bed for a child.

how_to_choose.title: Plan two activities a day at most
how_to_choose.text: One sight in the morning and one in the afternoon, with a long lunch and a rest, is the right rhythm for most families. Over-packed itineraries lead to tired, unhappy children. Build in a free afternoon in Pokhara for boating or the pool, and keep evenings short.

faqs.q: What is the cost of a Nepal family tour package from India?
faqs.a: A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan family package usually costs ₹28,000–45,000 per adult at 3-star, twin sharing, with lower rates for children sharing a room. At 5-star it starts around ₹95,000 per adult. Prices cover hotels, private transfers, sightseeing and the Chitwan safari; flights or train travel from your Indian city to Nepal are extra.

faqs.q: Is Nepal safe for a family holiday with young children?
faqs.a: Yes. Nepal is generally safe for families, and Nepali people are warm towards children. The main things to manage are road travel, food hygiene and altitude. Use a private car with seat belts, drink bottled or filtered water, choose freshly cooked food and keep overnight stays below about 2,500 m. Carry basic medicines, as pharmacies outside cities are limited.

faqs.q: Can children go on the Everest helicopter tour?
faqs.a: Children can join an Everest helicopter tour, but we suggest skipping the high landing at Kala Patthar (5,644 m) for under-tens and infants. A sensible alternative is a flight with breakfast at Hotel Everest View (3,880 m), where the stop is short. The Everest mountain flight by plane involves no altitude exposure and suits all ages.

faqs.q: What is the best time for a Nepal family holiday?
faqs.a: October to November is ideal, overlapping with Dussehra and Diwali holidays in India: clear skies, comfortable temperatures and festivals in full swing. March and April are also good. December and January are cold in the mornings but sunny. May and June suit Indian summer holidays, but expect heat in Chitwan and some haze over the mountains.

faqs.q: Do Indian children need a passport to travel to Nepal?
faqs.a: Indian children do not need a visa, and a passport is the simplest document. Children under 15 can usually travel with a photo ID showing age, such as a school ID or a birth certificate, and 15–18 year olds with an identity certificate from their school principal. Airlines can be stricter than land borders. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long should a family trip to Nepal be?
faqs.a: Six to eight nights is ideal for a first family visit: two or three nights in Kathmandu, two or three in Pokhara and two in Chitwan. With only four or five nights, choose two places rather than three. Add a night in Nagarkot or Bandipur for mountain views and a slower pace if your children enjoy walks.

name: Honeymoon in Nepal
tagline: Lake views, jungle lodges and Himalayan sunrises for two
meta_description: Honeymoon in Nepal: Kathmandu, Nagarkot, Pokhara and Chitwan packages for couples, with romantic hotels, best months, helicopter add-ons and prices.
summary: A Nepal honeymoon usually combines Kathmandu's old towns, Pokhara's lakeside and a jungle lodge in Chitwan over 6–7 nights, costing roughly ₹45,000–1,10,000 per person depending on hotel class. Add a sunrise night in Nagarkot or Dhulikhel, or a private helicopter breakfast facing Everest, for a trip that feels private rather than packaged.
intro: Most couples arrive in Kathmandu and spend two nights among the courtyards of Patan and Bhaktapur. Dwarika's Hotel, built around centuries-old carved woodwork, is the classic honeymoon stay in the city. From there, a night at Nagarkot (about 2,200 m) or Dhulikhel puts the Himalaya outside your window at sunrise, with the Langtang range and, on very clear days, peaks towards Everest on the horizon. Club Himalaya in Nagarkot and Dwarika's Resort in Dhulikhel are popular, quiet choices for couples. Kathmandu to Nagarkot is about 32 km and 1.5 hours by road.

Pokhara is the heart of most honeymoon itineraries. Couples row across Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi temple, watch sunrise from Sarangkot, paraglide in tandem and spend evenings at lakeside cafes. For a quieter stay, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge on a ridge east of the city and The Pavilions Himalayas in the countryside west of Pokhara offer privacy and views of Machhapuchhre. Lakeside hotels cost far less and keep you within walking distance of restaurants. A 6-night Kathmandu–Nagarkot–Pokhara honeymoon at good 4-star hotels costs about ₹55,000–75,000 per person.

Chitwan's jungle lodges suit couples who want something different from a beach. Barahi Jungle Lodge, Kasara Resort and Meghauli Serai offer private villas, riverside dinners and naturalist-led safaris. For a splurge, a private helicopter charter to the Everest region with breakfast at Hotel Everest View (3,880 m) costs about US$5,000–6,500 for up to five seats. October to April is the best window; December and January are cool and crisp with clear views, which suits the Indian winter wedding season. Monsoon honeymoons are cheaper but cloudier.

how_to_choose.title: Choose a pace for two
how_to_choose.text: Two nights per stop is the minimum for a relaxed honeymoon. Six nights works well for Kathmandu, Pokhara and one sunrise or jungle stay; eight nights lets you add Chitwan and Nagarkot without rushing. Fly Kathmandu–Pokhara and keep the saved day for yourselves.

how_to_choose.title: Spend on one special stay
how_to_choose.text: Rather than upgrading every night, many couples choose one standout property, such as Dwarika's in Kathmandu, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge or a Chitwan jungle lodge, and keep the rest at good 3- or 4-star hotels. The memory usually comes from the setting and the view rather than the room size.

how_to_choose.title: Add one shared adventure
how_to_choose.text: A tandem paragliding flight in Pokhara, a canoe ride in Chitwan, a short trek to Australian Camp or an Everest mountain flight gives you a story to share. Pick something both of you will enjoy; a sunrise boat on Phewa Lake can be as memorable as a helicopter.

how_to_choose.title: Mind the season and festivals
how_to_choose.text: October and November bring clear skies and Dashain and Tihar celebrations, but hotels fill early. December to February is quieter and suits winter weddings, though mornings are cold. April brings rhododendrons in the hills. Book Pokhara and Chitwan lodges two to three months ahead for peak dates.

faqs.q: How much does a Nepal honeymoon package cost?
faqs.a: A 6-night Nepal honeymoon costs roughly ₹45,000–60,000 per person at 3-star hotels, ₹55,000–75,000 at good 4-star hotels, and ₹1,00,000 or more at luxury properties such as Dwarika's and Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge, twin sharing. Prices include hotels, transfers and sightseeing. Flights to Kathmandu, adventure activities and special dinners are extra.

faqs.q: Which is better for a honeymoon, Pokhara or Nagarkot?
faqs.a: Do both if you can. Pokhara has the lake, cafes, boating and paragliding, and enough to fill two or three days. Nagarkot is a quiet hill station about 1.5 hours from Kathmandu, best for one night of sunrise and sunset views. If you must choose, Pokhara gives more variety; Nagarkot or Dhulikhel suit a short, peaceful add-on.

faqs.q: Is Nepal good for a honeymoon in December?
faqs.a: Yes. December brings dry, sunny days and some of the clearest mountain views of the year in Pokhara and Nagarkot, with Pokhara daytime temperatures around 18–20 °C. Nights and early mornings are cold, close to freezing in Nagarkot, so pack warm layers. Chitwan is foggy in the mornings. It is quieter than October and November, so rates are often lower.

faqs.q: Can we take a helicopter to Everest on our honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. A private Everest helicopter charter lets you choose your timing, land at Kala Patthar (5,644 m) for 10–15 minutes and have breakfast at Hotel Everest View facing Ama Dablam. It costs about US$5,000–6,500 for the helicopter, while a shared seat costs US$1,100–1,400 per person. Pregnant travellers should not fly to high altitude.

faqs.q: What are the best honeymoon hotels in Nepal?
faqs.a: Couples often choose Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu, Dwarika's Resort in Dhulikhel, Club Himalaya in Nagarkot, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge and The Pavilions Himalayas near Pokhara, and Barahi Jungle Lodge or Meghauli Serai in Chitwan. Good lakeside hotels in Pokhara cost far less. We match the hotel to your budget and the views you want.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for a Nepal honeymoon?
faqs.a: Six to seven nights is the sweet spot: two in Kathmandu, one in Nagarkot or Dhulikhel and three in Pokhara, or swap one Pokhara night for Chitwan. With five nights, keep it to Kathmandu and Pokhara. Ten nights lets you add a jungle lodge, Bandipur and a slow final day without packing every morning.

name: Luxury holidays in Nepal
tagline: Heritage hotels, private helicopters and lodges with views
meta_description: Luxury holidays in Nepal: Dwarika's, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge, Meghauli Serai, Shinta Mani Mustang and private Everest helicopters, with prices.
summary: Luxury travel in Nepal means heritage hotels in Kathmandu, view lodges above Pokhara, private jungle villas in Chitwan and private helicopters to Everest or Mustang. A 6-night 5-star circuit starts around ₹95,000 per person; with charters and top lodges, expect ₹2,50,000 or more. We plan private guides, cars and flexible timings throughout.
intro: In Kathmandu, Dwarika's Hotel sets the benchmark, with courtyards built from salvaged Newar carvings and a spa. International brands include the Hyatt Regency near Boudhanath and the Kathmandu Marriott, while Hotel Yak & Yeti occupies part of a Rana-era palace off Durbar Marg. Private guides take you into Patan and Bhaktapur before crowds arrive, and evenings can include a private Newari dinner. A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan circuit at 5-star typically starts at ₹95,000 per person, twin sharing, rising with suites, private flights and top lodges.

Outside the capital, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge and The Pavilions Himalayas offer private terraces facing the Annapurna range. In Chitwan, Meghauli Serai and Barahi Jungle Lodge run naturalist-led safaris and riverside dining. Shinta Mani Mustang in Jomsom, opened in 2023, brings high-end comfort to the Kali Gandaki valley at about 2,700 m, with jeep and helicopter excursions to Muktinath and Lo Manthang. In the Khumbu, Yeti Mountain Home lodges and Hotel Everest View let trekkers and helicopter guests stay in more comfort along the Everest trail.

Private helicopters change what is possible. A charter for up to five seats to Everest with a Kala Patthar landing costs about US$5,000–6,500, and similar charters reach Annapurna Base Camp, Muktinath or Upper Mustang in a morning. Helicopters fly only in good weather, usually early, and carry fewer passengers at high landings, so plans need a buffer day. Luxury in Nepal is also about service: a private car and driver, a guide who knows your interests, and flexible timing. The best months are October–November and March–April, when rooms book out early.

how_to_choose.title: Pick properties, then routes
how_to_choose.text: Nepal has a short list of truly high-end hotels, and they shape the itinerary. Start with the stays you want, such as Dwarika's, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge or Meghauli Serai, then plan transfers between them. Elsewhere, a good 4-star hotel is often the best option available.

how_to_choose.title: Fly private where roads are slow
how_to_choose.text: Kathmandu to Pokhara is 6–8 hours by road but 25 minutes by plane or about 40 minutes by private helicopter. For Chitwan, Mustang or the Everest region, charters remove early starts and connection risk. They cost more but buy back whole days on a short trip.

how_to_choose.title: Ask for private guiding
how_to_choose.text: A private guide and vehicle let you see Pashupatinath at dawn, linger in a Bhaktapur workshop or skip a site that does not interest you. We match guides to your interests, from Newar architecture to Buddhist art or birding, and build days around your pace rather than a group schedule.

how_to_choose.title: Book peak dates early
how_to_choose.text: Top lodges have few rooms. For October, November and the Diwali period, book four to six months ahead; for Christmas and New Year, at least three months. Helicopter charters can be arranged a few weeks out, but fixed dates in peak season are safer secured early.

faqs.q: What are the best luxury hotels in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Dwarika's Hotel is the best-known heritage luxury hotel, built around traditional Newar woodwork. Hyatt Regency Kathmandu, near Boudhanath, and the Kathmandu Marriott offer international five-star comfort, and Hotel Yak & Yeti sits partly in a Rana-era palace near Durbar Marg. Each has spas, good restaurants and easy access to the main heritage sites.

faqs.q: How much does a luxury Nepal tour cost?
faqs.a: A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan circuit at 5-star hotels starts around ₹95,000 per person, twin sharing, with private car and guide. Adding top lodges such as Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge or Meghauli Serai, domestic flights and a private Everest helicopter charter can take the total to ₹2,50,000–4,00,000 per person. We quote each element so you see where the money goes.

faqs.q: Is there a luxury lodge on the Everest trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Yeti Mountain Home runs comfortable lodges in the lower Khumbu, including Lukla, Phakding, Monjo, Namche Bazaar and Kongde, with attached bathrooms and better beds than standard teahouses. Hotel Everest View, at 3,880 m above Namche, is a well-known stop. Higher up, options are simpler, so luxury Everest trips often use a helicopter for the return.

faqs.q: Can we do Everest Base Camp in luxury?
faqs.a: Partly. Many travellers trek up to Namche Bazaar or Tengboche using upgraded lodges, continue to Base Camp on standard lodges and fly back by helicopter from Gorak Shep or Kala Patthar. Others skip trekking and take a private helicopter tour with a Kala Patthar landing and breakfast at Hotel Everest View. Both options depend on the weather.

faqs.q: Which months are best for a luxury holiday in Nepal?
faqs.a: October to November and March to April. Autumn gives the clearest mountain views and the main festival season; spring adds warmth and rhododendrons. December to February is excellent for Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan, with sunny days and cool nights. Book top lodges four to six months ahead for the peak months.

faqs.q: Is Shinta Mani Mustang worth it?
faqs.a: For travellers who want the Mustang landscape with high-end comfort, it is the main luxury option in the region. The lodge sits in Jomsom at about 2,700 m and arranges guided excursions by jeep and helicopter, including Muktinath and, with permits, Upper Mustang. It is expensive and the Jomsom flight depends on the weather, so allow a flexible day either side.

name: Budget Nepal tour packages
tagline: Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan without overspending
meta_description: Budget Nepal tour packages from India: Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan from ₹14,000, with road routes from the border, cheap seasons and money tips.
summary: Nepal is one of the most affordable foreign trips for Indian travellers. A 3-night Kathmandu break starts around ₹14,000 per person at 3-star, and a 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan loop from about ₹28,000. Travelling by road from the border, choosing shoulder months and sharing a car cut costs further without cutting the main sights.
intro: The biggest saving for Indian travellers is getting there. A return flight from Delhi to Kathmandu can cost more than the whole land package in peak season, while a train to Gorakhpur and a 95 km drive to the Sonauli border costs a fraction of that. From Belahiya on the Nepal side, Pokhara is about 185 km and 7–8 hours by road, and Kathmandu about 280 km and 8–10 hours. Many budget circuits therefore start at the border, visit Lumbini or Pokhara first and finish in Kathmandu before heading home.

Inside Nepal, standard 3-star hotels in Thamel and Pokhara Lakeside are clean and comfortable at modest rates, and twin sharing keeps per-person prices low. Tourist buses between Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan are cheap but slow; a shared private car is faster for families or groups of four. Dal bhat, momo and thukpa in local restaurants cost far less than hotel buffets, and dal bhat usually comes with free refills. Indian rupees are widely accepted, but carry ₹100 notes or smaller; rules on larger notes have changed, so check current status before you travel.

Timing matters as much as hotels. February, early March, late April to May and the first half of September usually have lower rates than the October–November peak, with decent weather. The monsoon, June to August, brings the lowest prices but cloudy mountains and road delays. Entry fees for Durbar Squares and parks are lower for SAARC nationals. A 3-night Kathmandu package costs ₹14,000–25,000, a 2-night Chitwan safari ₹12,000–20,000, and a 4–5 day Poon Hill trek from Pokhara roughly ₹25,000–40,000 per person with guide and permits.

how_to_choose.title: Travel overland from India
how_to_choose.text: If you live in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar or nearby, the train to Gorakhpur or Raxaul, or a bus to the border, is far cheaper than flying. Plan Lumbini, Pokhara and Chitwan from the border side, then decide whether to fly home from Kathmandu or return by road.

how_to_choose.title: Share a car, not a coach
how_to_choose.text: For two people, tourist buses are the cheapest way between Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan. For four to six, a shared private car often costs about the same per head, stops where you want and saves an hour or two each way. Ask us to compare both for your group.

how_to_choose.title: Travel in the shoulder months
how_to_choose.text: Late February to March and the first half of September often bring noticeably lower hotel rates than October and November, with good weather on most days. Avoid the Dashain, Diwali and Christmas weeks if price matters, as rooms and flights cost the most then.

how_to_choose.title: Pick 3-star hotels, eat local
how_to_choose.text: A clean 3-star hotel with breakfast is all you need in Kathmandu and Pokhara, since you will be out most of the day. Eat dal bhat, momo and Newari snacks in local restaurants, and save hotel dinners for one evening. Carry a refillable bottle and use filtered water stations.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Nepal tour package from India?
faqs.a: The cheapest options are 3-night Kathmandu breaks from about ₹14,000 per person at 3-star, or road trips from the Sonauli border covering Lumbini and Pokhara over 4–5 nights in a similar range. Travel from your home city to Kathmandu or the border is extra. Group departures and shoulder months bring prices down further.

faqs.q: How much money do I need per day in Nepal?
faqs.a: On a budget, plan about ₹2,500–4,000 per person per day for a shared 3-star twin room, local meals and city transport, excluding tours and long transfers. Entry fees to heritage sites and parks add more. On treks, budget around ₹2,000–3,500 per day for lodges and meals, plus your guide's wages if they are not already included.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to go to Nepal by road or by air?
faqs.a: By road is almost always cheaper for travellers from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. A train to Gorakhpur plus a car to Sonauli costs a small part of a peak-season flight. From Mumbai, Bengaluru or Chennai, compare carefully: a 30–40 hour train journey may save money but costs two days each way. Flights booked early can be reasonable.

faqs.q: Can I use Indian rupees in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian rupees are widely accepted in Nepal at the fixed rate of ₹100 to NPR 160, and many shops, hotels and taxis take them directly. Carry ₹100 notes and smaller where possible, as rules on ₹200 and ₹500 notes have changed in recent years. Some merchants now accept UPI payments from Indian apps. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is a budget trek in Nepal safe?
faqs.a: Yes, if you do not cut corners on the essentials. Choose a licensed guide, which is now required on most trekking routes for foreigners, carry insurance that covers helicopter rescue, and do not skip acclimatisation days to save money. Budget savings should come from simple lodges and local food, not from rushing the itinerary.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest time to visit Nepal?
faqs.a: June to August, during the monsoon, has the lowest hotel rates and fewest visitors, but mountain views are often hidden and roads suffer landslides. For a balance of price and weather, choose late February to March or the first two weeks of September. December and January are also good value for Kathmandu and Pokhara.

name: Buddhist circuit tours in Nepal
tagline: Lumbini, Kapilavastu, Boudhanath and the Buddha's Nepal
meta_description: Buddhist circuit tours in Nepal: Lumbini, Kapilavastu, Ramagrama, Boudhanath and Namo Buddha, linked with Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar in India.
summary: Nepal's Buddhist circuit starts at Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, and continues to Tilaurakot, Ramagrama, Kathmandu's great stupas and Namo Buddha. Many pilgrims link it with Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar in India, crossing at Sonauli. A 3–4 night Nepal section from the border is easy to plan and good value.
intro: Lumbini, about 20 km from Bhairahawa near the Sonauli border, is where Queen Maya Devi gave birth to Siddhartha Gautama. The Maya Devi Temple protects the marker stone, beside the sacred pool and the pillar raised by Emperor Ashoka in about 249 BCE. North of the sacred garden, the monastic zone holds monasteries built by Buddhist communities from Thailand, Myanmar, Germany, China, Japan and elsewhere, linked by a long canal. Lumbini is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and two nights let you see it unhurried, by bicycle or electric rickshaw.

Around Lumbini lie the places of the Buddha's early life. Tilaurakot, about 27 km west, is identified by many archaeologists as the palace of King Suddhodana in ancient Kapilavastu. Ramagrama, east of Lumbini, holds an unopened relic stupa, and Devdaha is linked to Maya Devi's family. From Lumbini, Kushinagar in India, where the Buddha died, is about 170 km and 4–5 hours by road through Sonauli, while Bodh Gaya and Sarnath connect via Gorakhpur. Most Buddhist circuit groups spend 3–4 nights in Nepal within a 10–14 day India–Nepal itinerary.

Kathmandu has the other great Buddhist sites. Boudhanath, one of the largest stupas in South Asia, is ringed by Tibetan monasteries, and Swayambhunath watches the valley from its hilltop. Namo Buddha, about 40 km east near Dhulikhel, marks the legend of the prince who fed a starving tigress, with Thrangu Tashi Yangtse Monastery above it. Kopan Monastery runs meditation courses, including its well-known November course. Pokhara's World Peace Pagoda and the monasteries of Mustang extend the route. October to March is the best season; Buddha Jayanti falls in April or May.

how_to_choose.title: Link Nepal with India's sites
how_to_choose.text: If Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar are on your list, enter Nepal at Sonauli and spend two nights in Lumbini, then either return to India or continue to Kathmandu. A full India–Nepal circuit takes 10–14 days; the Nepal section adds 3–5 days to it.

how_to_choose.title: Give Lumbini two nights
how_to_choose.text: The sacred garden, the monastic zone, Tilaurakot and Ramagrama are spread out. One night allows a rushed visit; two nights let you see the Maya Devi Temple at dawn, cycle between monasteries and visit Kapilavastu without hurry. Simple and mid-range hotels sit near the main gate.

how_to_choose.title: Plan around the Terai heat
how_to_choose.text: Lumbini lies low on the Terai plains and is very hot from April to June, often above 38 °C. October to March is far more comfortable, though December and January mornings bring dense fog that can delay flights into Bhairahawa. Visit the gardens early in the day.

how_to_choose.title: Add meditation or monastery stays
how_to_choose.text: For a spiritual focus, add a meditation course at Kopan Monastery in Kathmandu or quiet days at Namo Buddha. Some monasteries in the Lumbini monastic zone also offer meditation sessions. Course dates and guest rules vary, so confirm well ahead and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Lumbini from the Indian border?
faqs.a: Lumbini is about 25–30 km from the Sonauli–Belahiya border, around 45 minutes to an hour by road via Bhairahawa. Gorakhpur, the nearest major Indian railhead, is about 95 km from Sonauli, so Gorakhpur to Lumbini takes about 3–4 hours including the border. Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa is about 20 km from Lumbini.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Lumbini?
faqs.a: Two nights is ideal. The first day covers the Maya Devi Temple, the Ashoka pillar, the sacred pool and the main monasteries in the monastic zone. The second day lets you visit Tilaurakot and Ramagrama, or return to the garden at dawn. One night works if you are on a tight India–Nepal circuit.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Lumbini?
faqs.a: October to March is best, with pleasant days of about 20–28 °C. December and January can bring thick morning fog. April to June is very hot, often above 38 °C, though Buddha Jayanti in April or May draws pilgrims despite the heat. The monsoon, from late June to September, brings heavy rain and humidity.

faqs.q: Can I do the Buddhist circuit from Varanasi to Lumbini?
faqs.a: Yes. From Varanasi, visit Sarnath, then drive to Kushinagar in about 6–7 hours and on to Lumbini via Gorakhpur and Sonauli in another 4–5 hours. Alternatively, take a train from Varanasi to Gorakhpur and drive from there. Buddha Air has flown Varanasi to Kathmandu, which helps if you want to finish in Kathmandu; schedules change.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a passport to visit Lumbini?
faqs.a: No visa is needed. Indian citizens can cross into Nepal at Sonauli with a valid passport or Voter ID card, and either works for hotel check-in in Lumbini. Children need photo ID showing their age. Aadhaar is not accepted as a travel document for adults. Rules can change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What Buddhist sites are there in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: The main ones are Boudhanath Stupa, with its Tibetan monasteries and evening kora, and Swayambhunath on its hilltop west of the city. Namo Buddha, about 40 km east, is a quiet pilgrimage site with a large monastery. Kopan Monastery offers meditation courses, and Patan has old Newar Buddhist courtyards such as the Golden Temple, Hiranya Varna Mahavihar.

name: Yoga and wellness retreats in Nepal
tagline: Yoga, meditation and quiet mountain retreats
meta_description: Yoga and wellness retreats in Nepal: Pokhara yoga holidays, Kopan meditation courses, Dhulikhel spa resorts and hot springs, with costs and seasons.
summary: Nepal's wellness retreats centre on Pokhara and the hills around Kathmandu, where yoga and meditation programmes of 3–14 days run in lakeside or ridge-top settings. We add spa stays at Dhulikhel and Kathmandu, meditation courses at monasteries such as Kopan, and natural hot springs on the Annapurna trails.
intro: Pokhara is the most popular base for yoga in Nepal. Retreat centres line the quieter north and west shores of Phewa Lake and the slopes towards Sarangkot, offering daily hatha or vinyasa classes, pranayama and simple vegetarian meals with views of Machhapuchhre. Programmes range from drop-in classes to 7–14 day courses and longer teacher training. Simple retreats often cost roughly US$40–80 per day including room and meals, while resort-style programmes cost far more. October to December and February to April give the clearest mornings for outdoor practice.

Around Kathmandu, Kopan Monastery on a hill north of Boudhanath runs introductory Buddhist meditation courses, including its long November course. Nagarkot and Dhulikhel on the valley rim offer fresh air at about 1,500–2,200 m and quiet resort stays; Dwarika's Resort in Dhulikhel focuses on wellness programmes, yoga and spa therapies. Namo Buddha nearby suits travellers who want silence among monasteries and forest. Course dates, rules on phones and silence, and fees vary from place to place, so confirm well ahead and plan the rest of your trip around them.

Nepal also offers wellness in its landscapes. Natural hot springs sit along popular trails, including Jhinu Danda on the Annapurna Base Camp route and Tatopani on the Kali Gandaki below Ghorepani. Gentle treks such as Poon Hill combine walking with sunrise over Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South. For Indian guests, a 4–5 night Pokhara yoga holiday fits easily into a week, and Lumbini adds a meditation focus in the Buddha's birthplace. Wellness stays work year-round, though monsoon rain in July and August limits outdoor sessions and hides the mountains.

how_to_choose.title: Choose your style of practice
how_to_choose.text: Decide whether you want daily yoga classes with free time, a structured detox or Ayurveda programme, or silent meditation. Pokhara suits yoga holidays with sightseeing, Kopan and Namo Buddha suit Buddhist meditation, and Dhulikhel resorts suit spa-focused breaks with some yoga.

how_to_choose.title: Check teacher credentials
how_to_choose.text: Look for teachers with recognised training, such as Yoga Alliance registration or long study in India or Nepal, and a clear daily schedule. Ask how many students share a class and whether beginners are welcome. Detailed feedback from past students tells you more than a brochure does.

how_to_choose.title: Plan the length honestly
how_to_choose.text: Three days gives a taste; seven days lets a routine settle; 10–14 day courses suit those wanting real change. If you are combining a retreat with sightseeing, put the retreat at the end of the trip so you leave rested rather than rushing back into tours.

how_to_choose.title: Know the rules before you book
how_to_choose.text: Many retreats ask for no alcohol, vegetarian meals, early rising and limited phone use; meditation courses at monasteries may require silence and full attendance. Read the rules carefully, especially for Kopan, where places in popular courses fill months in advance. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where is the best place for a yoga retreat in Nepal?
faqs.a: Pokhara is the most popular, with many retreat centres around Phewa Lake and on the hills towards Sarangkot, and mountain views from outdoor practice halls. Kathmandu's valley rim, at Nagarkot and Dhulikhel, suits shorter stays and spa breaks. For Buddhist meditation rather than yoga, Kopan Monastery and Namo Buddha near Kathmandu are the usual choices.

faqs.q: How much does a yoga retreat in Nepal cost?
faqs.a: Simple retreats in Pokhara often cost roughly US$40–80 per day, including a shared or private room, two yoga sessions and vegetarian meals. Resort wellness programmes at places like Dwarika's Resort in Dhulikhel cost much more. Teacher training courses are priced separately. Travel to Pokhara and any sightseeing are extra.

faqs.q: Can beginners join a yoga retreat in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. Most Pokhara retreats welcome beginners and adapt postures to each student, often running mixed-level classes. Tell the retreat about injuries or health conditions in advance. Silent meditation courses are also open to beginners, though they demand discipline. If unsure, start with a 3–5 day programme before committing to a longer course.

faqs.q: What is the Kopan Monastery November course?
faqs.a: Kopan Monastery, north of Boudhanath in Kathmandu, runs an annual month-long introductory course in Buddhist philosophy and meditation each November, alongside shorter courses during the year. It includes teachings, meditation sessions and periods of silence, with simple accommodation at the monastery. Places fill well in advance; check dates and current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Are there hot springs in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. The best known for travellers are at Jhinu Danda on the Annapurna Base Camp trek, about 20 minutes' walk down to the river, and Tatopani on the Kali Gandaki, which is reachable by road from Beni. Both are simple pools rather than spas, and make a good rest stop after a few days of walking.

faqs.q: When is the best time for a wellness holiday in Nepal?
